title: The Sunday Read: ‘The Bodily Indignities of the Space Life’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片盛行的时代，当我还在夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，把 DJ 台变成了一个充满美妙的 50 年前老物件的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, this is The Sunday Read.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是“周日悦读”。

sentences.en: My name is Kim Tingley and I'm a contributing writer to The New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是金·廷利，《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: This week's episode is a story of mine from the magazine's recent issue devoted to outer space.
sentences.zh: 本期的节目是我的一个故事，选自该杂志最近一期以太空为主题的专刊。

sentences.en: And my story is about what happens to us, to the human body, once we leave planet Earth.
sentences.zh: 我的故事讲的是当我们离开地球后，我们身上——也就是人类的身体——会发生什么。

sentences.en: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin went up to space in 1961.
sentences.zh: 苏联宇航员尤里·加加林于 1961 年飞向太空。

sentences.en: Although we'd sent up animals before, at that time, we were still really unsure what would happen to people in low gravity.
sentences.zh: 尽管此前我们已经送过动物上太空，但在当时，我们仍然很不确定人类在低重力环境下会发生什么。

sentences.en: Unsure about even the basics.
sentences.zh: 甚至连最基本的事情都不确定。

sentences.en: Would you be able to swallow?
sentences.zh: 你能吞咽吗？

sentences.en: Would you choke on your own tongue?
sentences.zh: 你会不会被自己的舌头噎住？

sentences.en: As it turned out, during his 108-minute orbit around Earth, Yuri Gagarin could eat and drink just fine.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在围绕地球飞行 108 分钟的过程中，尤里·加加林吃喝一切正常。

sentences.en: We learned from his short journey that we could go up there and back, and that some of our basic functions would be okay.
sentences.zh: 我们从他的短途旅行中得知，我们可以去太空并返回，并且我们的一些基本机能会没问题。

sentences.en: And so, we sent more people up, farther away and for longer periods of time, first to the moon, and later to the International Space Station.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们送了更多的人去更远的地方、停留更长的时间，首先是月球，后来是国际空间站。

sentences.en: Fewer than 700 people have been to space.
sentences.zh: 去过太空的人不到 700。

sentences.en: It may sound like a lot, but it's not enough to draw conclusions about what long-term space habitation would do to people.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能很多，但还不足以得出关于长期太空居住会对人类产生什么影响的结论。

sentences.en: Astronauts have tended to be a pretty homogenous group.
sentences.zh: 宇航员往往是一个相当同质化的群体。

sentences.en: They're physically fit.
sentences.zh: 他们的身体都很健康。

sentences.en: They're ultra-healthy individuals.
sentences.zh: 他们都是超级健康的人。

sentences.en: And so, they're definitely not a representative sample of the human race.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们绝对不是人类的代表性样本。

sentences.en: What we do know is our bodies can adapt pretty quickly to space.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，我们的身体可以很快适应太空。

sentences.en: At first, you might get a kind of space car sickness, something called space adaptation syndrome, which will eventually go away.
sentences.zh: 起初，你可能会得一种太空晕车病，也就是所谓的太空适应综合症，但它最终会消失。

sentences.en: But then, your body will begin diverting resources away from your bones and muscles because they no longer need to support your weight.
sentences.zh: 但随后，你的身体会开始将资源从骨骼和肌肉中转移出去，因为它们不再需要支撑你的体重。

sentences.en: Your blood and other fluids no longer have to fight gravity, so they shift upwards.
sentences.zh: 你的血液和其他体液不再需要对抗重力，所以它们会向上转移。

sentences.en: Your face becomes bloated, and you sort of get chicken legs.
sentences.zh: 你的脸会浮肿，你的腿会变得像鸡腿一样细。

sentences.en: The longest anyone's ever been in space is 437 days.
sentences.zh: 人类在太空呆的最长时间是 437 天。

sentences.en: But long-term, what we don't know is this.
sentences.zh: 但在长期来看，我们所不知道的是这些。

sentences.en: Say that we're out there for years.
sentences.zh: 假设我们在外面待上好几年。

sentences.en: Would our bodies ever change to the point when we wouldn't even be able to return to Earth?
sentences.zh: 我们的身体会发生变化，甚至连回到地球都做不到了吗？

sentences.en: And at that point, would we become something else?
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，我们会变成别的东西吗？

sentences.en: Entirely?
sentences.zh: 完全变成别的？

sentences.en: So, here's my article.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: The Bodily Indignities of the Space Life.
sentences.zh: 太空生活的身体尊严丧失。

sentences.en: Read by Julia Whelan.
sentences.zh: 由朱莉娅·韦兰朗读。

sentences.en: Our audio producer today is Jack Desidoro.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的音频制作人是杰克·德西多罗。

sentences.en: The original music for this episode was written and performed by Aaron Esposito.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的原创音乐由阿伦·埃斯波西托创作并演奏。

sentences.en: As an incubator of life, Earth has a lot going for it, something we often fail to appreciate fully from within its nurturing bounds.
sentences.zh: 作为生命的孵化器，地球有着诸多优势，这是我们在它滋养的边界之内时经常未能充分体会的。

sentences.en: Merely sending probes and rovers to the moon and Mars won't do.
sentences.zh: 仅仅向月球和火星发送探测器和漫游车是远远不够的。

sentences.en: For various reasons—adventure, apocalypse, commerce—we insist upon taking our corporeal selves off-world, too.
sentences.zh: 出于各种原因——冒险、末日、商业——我们坚持把我们有血有肉的身体也带离这个世界。

sentences.en: Multiple private companies have announced plans to put hotels in space soon.
sentences.zh: 多家私营公司已经宣布了不久将在太空建造酒店的计划。

sentences.en: NASA is aiming to 3D-print lunar neighborhoods within a couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 美国宇航局的目标是在几十年内在月球上用 3D 打印建造居民区。

sentences.en: And while it will probably take longer than that to build and populate an outpost on Mars, preparations are being made.
sentences.zh: 虽然建造和填充火星前哨站可能需要更长的时间，但各项筹备工作正在进行中。

sentences.en: This summer, four NASA crew members began a 378-day stay in simulated Martian housing at the Johnson Space Center in Houston.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，四名美国宇航局乘员开始在休斯顿约翰逊航天中心的模拟火星住宅中进行为期 378 天的居住。

sentences.en: When you look at the renderings of these cozy dwellings, it's easy to lose sight of how hostile space is to Earthlings.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这些舒适住宅的效果图时，你很容易忽视太空对地球人来说是多么充满敌意。

sentences.en: As a reminder, consider what would happen if you found yourself in low Earth orbit or on Mars or the moon without a spacesuit on.
sentences.zh: 作为提醒，想想如果你不穿宇航服就发现自己处于近地轨道、火星或月球上会发生什么。

sentences.en: You would pass out from a lack of oxygen within a matter of seconds, a condition known as hypoxia, and die soon thereafter.
sentences.zh: 你会在几秒钟内因缺氧而晕倒，这种情况被称为缺氧症，随后不久就会死亡。

sentences.en: In the brief meantime, all the gases inside your body, including any air still in your lungs, would expand in the absence of external pressure.
sentences.zh: 在此期间的短短时间内，你体内的所有气体，包括肺部残留的任何空气，都会在没有外部压力的影响下膨胀。

sentences.en: Depressurization would also cause your internal fluids to bubble, not because they're heating up, but because they are transmogrifying into their gaseous state.
sentences.zh: 减压还会导致你的体内液体冒泡，这不是因为它们在变热，而是因为它们正在转化为气态。

sentences.en: The temperature wouldn't be much of a problem, at least, even though thermometers in low Earth orbit produce readings from minus 85 degrees to 257 degrees Fahrenheit,
sentences.zh: 温度不会成为太大的问题，至少不会，尽管近地轨道上的温度计读数从零下 85 度到 257 华氏度不等，

sentences.en: depending on whether they are in shadow or in light.
sentences.zh: 这取决于它们是在阴影中还是在光照下。

sentences.en: Space, as a near vacuum, has very little mass to conduct heat to or away from you, so you are not likely to feel instantly hot or cold.
sentences.zh: 太空作为一个接近真空的环境，几乎没有质量来向你传导热量或带走热量，所以你不太可能立即感到冷或热。

sentences.en: While hypoxia is potentially a real threat should your space vessel or extraterrestrial habitat leak, it's a manageable one,
sentences.zh: 虽然如果你的太空飞船或外星栖息地发生泄漏，缺氧可能是一个真正的威胁，但这是一个可以应对的威胁，

sentences.en: assuming you haven't leaped naked out of your space capsule or off-world dwelling.
sentences.zh: 前提是你没有赤身裸体地跳出太空舱或离地住所。

sentences.en: But two other major challenges confront our fragile bodies when we leave our planet, neither of which has been entirely solved yet, even indoors.
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们离开我们的星球时，我们的脆弱身体还要面对另外两个重大挑战，这两个挑战即使在室内也都没有完全解决。

sentences.en: Variable gravity and radiation.
sentences.zh: 可变重力和辐射。

sentences.en: Gravity is determined by the mass of objects and their distance from one another.
sentences.zh: 重力由物体的质量及其彼此之间的距离决定。

sentences.en: Because Earth is so big, it is impossible, while on it, to escape its gravity for any serious length of time.
sentences.zh: 因为地球如此巨大，当身处其上时，不可能在任何实质性的时间内逃脱它的重力。

sentences.en: As a result, we don't know very much about what our lives would be like without or under some diminished influence of this omnipresent attraction.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于没有这种无处不在的吸引力，或者在某种减弱的影响下，我们的生活会是什么样子，我们知之甚少。

sentences.en: On the Moon and on Mars, which are smaller than our world, the gravitational tug will be much less, a sixth and a third, respectively, of what it is here.
sentences.zh: 在比我们的世界更小的月球和火星上，引力拉扯将小得多，分别只有这里的六分之一和三分之一。

sentences.en: Conversely, radiation exposure intensifies with elevation, because there's less atmosphere above you to block it,
sentences.zh: 相反，辐射暴露会随着海拔的升高而加剧，因为你上方阻挡它的大气层变少了，

sentences.en: and you incur a much larger dose if you get beyond the protective bubble of Earth's ozone and magnetosphere,
sentences.zh: 如果你超越了地球臭氧层和磁层的保护气泡，你将承受大得多的剂量，

sentences.en: the magnetic field that stretches roughly 40,000 miles out at its most compressed point.
sentences.zh: 磁层在其受压缩最严重的地方向外延伸约 40,000 英里。

sentences.en: The solar and galactic radiation that washes over Mars, which at its closest is 34 million miles away,
sentences.zh: 冲刷着火星的太阳和银河辐射——火星在最近时距离我们 3400 万英里——

sentences.en: will potentially be 700 times as great as what passes through our magnetic defenses.
sentences.zh: 其威力可能是穿透我们磁场防御的辐射的 700 倍。

sentences.en: Space travelers beyond low Earth orbit will also be bombarded with high-energy atomic nuclei from exploding stars throughout the galaxy,
sentences.zh: 近地轨道以外的太空旅行者也将受到来自整个银河系爆炸恒星的高能原子核的轰击，

sentences.en: which are normally deflected by the magnetosphere from reaching the surface of our planet.
sentences.zh: 这些原子核通常会被磁层偏转，而无法到达我们星球的表面。

sentences.en: Those particles are so heavy and moving so fast that they penetrate spaceships, spacesuits, and skin,
sentences.zh: 这些粒子非常重，移动速度极快，它们会穿透飞船、宇航服和皮肤，

sentences.en: banging into other particles in their path and damaging any attendant cells in ways researchers are only beginning to understand.
sentences.zh: 撞击它们路径上的其他粒子，并以研究人员才刚刚开始了解的方式破坏任何伴随的细胞。

sentences.en: So far, most of what we know about the effects on the human body of these threats comes from astronauts in low Earth orbit,
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我们对人体受这些威胁影响的大部分了解来自于近地轨道的宇航员，

sentences.en: and because safety is a paramount concern, we don't send many of them up there, and we don't let them stay for long when we do.
sentences.zh: 由于安全是首要考虑的问题，我们不会送很多宇航员上去，当我们这样做时，也不会让他们停留太久。

sentences.en: Six months is the average length of a visit to the International Space Station, and fewer than 300 people have made the 250-mile voyage.
sentences.zh: 对国际空间站的访问平均长度为六个月，不到 300 人进行过这 250 英里的航行。

sentences.en: While that collective experience is enough to have taught us how the body responds when gravity's pull is substantially reduced, the magnetosphere still shields the ISS,
sentences.zh: 虽然这些集体的经验足以让我们了解当重力明显减弱时身体是如何反应的，但磁层仍然在保护着国际空间站，

sentences.en: and only the 24 astronauts who flew in the Apollo program have gone beyond it.
sentences.zh: 而且只有参加阿波罗计划的 24 名宇航员超越了它。

sentences.en: The moon orbits an average of more than 238,000 miles away.
sentences.zh: 月球的平均轨道距离超过 238,000 英里。

sentences.en: Though these two dozen astronauts spent little more than a week at a time without its protection, they have died of cardiovascular disease at a rate four to five times as high
sentences.zh: 尽管这二十四名宇航员在没有月球保护的情况下每次只呆了一个多星期，但他们死于心血管疾病的比率是

sentences.en: as that of their counterparts who stayed in low Earth orbit or never entered orbit at all,
sentences.zh: 留在近地轨道或从未进入轨道的人的同行们的四到五倍，

sentences.en: which suggests that exposure to cosmic radiation might have damaged their arteries, veins, and capillaries.
sentences.zh: 这表明接触宇宙辐射可能已经损坏了他们的动脉、静脉和毛细血管。

sentences.en: We can't send people to Mars or to live on the moon until we can be reasonably confident that they'll survive getting and residing there.
sentences.zh: 在我们能够合理确信他们能够到达并居住在那里并生存下来之前，我们不能把人送到火星或送去月球居住。

sentences.en: But the space-based medical science needed to make that possible has been hindered by small sample sizes that aren't representative of the general population.
sentences.zh: 但是，实现这一目标所需的基于太空的医学科学一直受到样本量小且不能代表普通人群的阻碍。

sentences.en: All of the Apollo astronauts were white men born between 1928 and 1936.
sentences.zh: 所有的阿波罗宇航员都是 1928 年至 1936 年间出生的白人男性。

sentences.en: Space tourism, though, promises to offer opportunities to study the effects of radiation and low gravity on a much broader demographic than really well-selected superpeople,
sentences.zh: 然而，太空旅游有望提供机会，研究辐射和低重力对比精心挑选的超级人类更广泛的人口统计学影响，

sentences.en: as Dorit Donneville, the director of the Translational Research Institute for Space Health,
sentences.zh: 正如太空健康转化研究所的所长多丽特·多内维尔所说，

sentences.en: Trish, at the Baylor College of Medicine, describes those who have historically qualified to leave the planet.
sentences.zh: 特里什，在贝勒医学院，形容那些历史上符合离开星球资格的人。

sentences.en: Old, young, pre-existing health conditions?
sentences.zh: 老人、年轻人、已有健康状况的人？

sentences.en: We are starting to gather a knowledge base that in the future will be essential even for NASA,
sentences.zh: 我们正在开始收集未来甚至对美国宇航局也至关重要的知识库，

sentences.en: Donneville told me.
sentences.zh: 多内维尔告诉我。

sentences.en: Because we have to learn about the edge cases to really understand what is going on in our bodies to adapt to a hostile environment.
sentences.zh: 因为我们必须了解极端情况，才能真正了解我们的身体内部发生了什么，以适应充满敌意的环境。

sentences.en: You don't learn as much from people who are healthy.
sentences.zh: 你从健康的人身上学不到那么多。

sentences.en: It's when people get sick that you understand how people get sick and how to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 只有当人们生病时，你才能明白人们是如何生病的以及如何预防它。

sentences.en: Epidemiologists face the same predicament on Earth.
sentences.zh: 流行病学家在地球上也面临着同样的困境。

sentences.en: Before they can figure out how to protect the population, they must wait for harm to come to enough people to expose the causes.
sentences.zh: 在他们弄清楚如何保护大众之前，他们必须等待伤害降临到足够多的人身上以暴露出原因。

sentences.en: As less rigorous medical screening allows more tourists to reach space, the chances increase significantly that someone will get hurt or have a health emergency there.
sentences.zh: 随着不太严格的医疗筛查允许更多的游客到达太空，有人受伤或在那里发生医疗紧急情况的机会显著增加。

sentences.en: Aerospace medicine is one of three specialties certified by the American Board of Preventive Medicine because surgeons for a given flight tend to be stuck on the ground.
sentences.zh: 航空航天医学是美国预防医学委员会认证的三大专业之一，因为特定飞行的外科医生往往被困在地面上。

sentences.en: They have to optimize the health of their patients and ward off potential disasters before departure.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在出发前优化患者的健康状况并防范潜在的灾难。

sentences.en: The problem is, they can't know what those disasters will be until they occur, which means that, as with every expedition into the unknown,
sentences.zh: 问题是，在灾难发生之前，他们无法知道这些灾难会是什么，这意味着，就像每一次对未知的探险一样，

sentences.en: at some point, some intrepid or desperate souls are just going to have to blast off and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，一些勇敢或绝望的灵魂将不得不直接起飞，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Scientists once predicted that we couldn't live in the absence of Earth's gravity.
sentences.zh: 科学家曾经预测，在没有地球重力的情况下我们无法生活。

sentences.en: Without this still barely understood force pulling us downward, how would we swallow?
sentences.zh: 如果没有这种仍然几乎不被理解的力把我们往下拉，我们该如何吞咽？

sentences.en: Wouldn't our tongues lull back into our throats?
sentences.zh: 我们的舌头难道不会无力地缩回喉咙里吗？

sentences.en: Wouldn't we choke on our own saliva?
sentences.zh: 我们难道不会被自己的唾液噎住吗？

sentences.en: And if we survived those perils, wouldn't escalating pressure in our skulls kill us after a week or so?
sentences.zh: 如果我们从这些危险中幸存下来，头骨内不断升高的压力难道不会在一个星期左右后杀死我们吗？

sentences.en: But when Yuri Gagarin returned from his single 108-minute orbit around our world in 1961, humanity's first trip beyond the mesosphere,
sentences.zh: 但当尤里·加加林于 1961 年从围绕我们世界的单次 108 分钟轨道飞行中返回时，这是人类对中层大气以外的首次旅行，

sentences.en: he proved that our internal musculature could maintain our vital functions in conditions of weightlessness.
sentences.zh: 他证明了我们的内部肌肉可以在失重状态下维持我们的生命机能。

sentences.en: He ate and drank up there without difficulty.
sentences.zh: 他在太空中毫无困难地吃喝。

sentences.en: Technically, he hadn't escaped Earth's influence.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，他并没有逃脱地球的影响。

sentences.en: To orbit is to freefall toward the ground without ever hitting it, and he was in a condition known as microgravity.
sentences.zh: 轨道飞行就是向地面自由落体却永远不会撞击地面，他处于一种被称为微重力的状态。

sentences.en: This felt, he reported, like hanging horizontally on belts, as if in a suspended state,
sentences.zh: 据他报告，这感觉就像水平挂在安全带上，仿佛处于一种悬浮状态，

sentences.en: a circumstance passingly familiar to anyone who has been on a roller coaster or jumped off a diving board.
sentences.zh: 这种环境对任何坐过过山车或从跳水板上跳下来的人来说都是顺便熟悉的。

sentences.en: Gagarin said he got used to it.
sentences.zh: 加加林说他已经习惯了。

sentences.en: There were no bad sensations, he added.
sentences.zh: 他补充说，没有任何不好的感觉。

sentences.en: Either Gagarin was fibbing, or he had a strong stomach.
sentences.zh: 要么加加林在撒谎，要么他的胃很好。

sentences.en: Initially, many space travelers puke, or at least feel motion sick.
sentences.zh: 最初，许多太空旅行者会呕吐，或者至少会感到晕动症。

sentences.en: Space Adaptation Syndrome, or SAS, is what such nausea, headache, and vomiting are called outside our atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 太空适应综合症，简称 SAS，就是这种恶心、头痛和呕吐在大气层之外的称呼。

sentences.en: It's the same as sitting in the back of the car in childhood, reading something with your head down,
sentences.zh: 这就像童年时坐在汽车后座，低着头看东西一样，

sentences.en: says Jan Stepanek, director of the Aerospace Medicine Program at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 位于亚利桑那州斯科茨代尔的妙佑医疗国际航空航天医学项目主任扬·斯捷潘内克说。

sentences.en: It's a mismatch of what the eyes are seeing and what the inner ear is telling you.
sentences.zh: 这是眼睛看到的和内耳告诉你的信息不匹配。

sentences.en: Only, in this case, that mismatched perception is a result of the organs and hairs of the vestibular system floating free without their usual gravitational signals.
sentences.zh: 只不过，在这种情况下，这种不匹配的感知是前庭系统的器官和毛发在没有通常重力信号的情况下自由漂浮的结果。

sentences.en: You acclimate eventually.
sentences.zh: 你最终会适应的。

sentences.en: In fact, researchers only learned about the prevalence of SAS symptoms in the 1970s, when they heard Skylab astronauts talking about it with one another over a hot mic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，研究人员直到 20 世纪 70 年代才了解到 SAS 症状的普遍性，当时他们听到太空实验室的宇航员在一个热麦克风上彼此谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Astronauts, it turns out, are not ideal subjects for medical study, because they are notoriously stoic and unforthcoming about any symptom that might ground them.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，宇航员并不是医学研究的理想受试者，因为他们出了名的坚忍，对任何可能让他们停飞的症状都三缄其口。

sentences.en: On Earth, your body maintains your blood pressure such that enough oxygen reaches your organs and waste is ferried away.
sentences.zh: 在地球上，你的身体维持着你的血压，以便足够的氧气到达你的器官，废物被运走。

sentences.en: One of the biggest oxygen users, your brain, is positioned above your heart for much of the time you are awake.
sentences.zh: 你清醒的大部分时间里，最大的耗氧器之一——你的大脑，都位于你的心脏上方。

sentences.en: But microgravity suddenly stops pulling blood downward into your legs, just as lying down or getting into a pool does, except more so.
sentences.zh: 但微重力突然停止将血液向下拽入你的腿部，就像躺下或跳进泳池一样，只是程度更深。

sentences.en: That lets blood collect in the upper body, triggering pressure sensors in your heart and the carotid vessels of your neck,
sentences.zh: 这让血液在上半身积聚，触发了你心脏和颈部颈动脉中的压力传感器，

sentences.en: which then send hormonal instructions to urinate more and decrease blood production.
sentences.zh: 然后它们会发送荷尔蒙指令，要求排尿更多并减少血液产生。

sentences.en: This is why you often feel the need to pee shortly after climbing into bed or sinking into a body of water.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你经常在爬上床或沉入水体后不久就感到有尿意。

sentences.en: On our planet, that's usually enough to reduce your blood pressure and rebalance the system.
sentences.zh: 在我们星球上，这通常足以降低你的血压并重新平衡系统。

sentences.en: In microgravity, however, the blood volume above your neck will most likely still be too high, at least for a while.
sentences.zh: 然而，在微重力下，你颈部以上的血容量很可能仍然过高，至少有一段时间是这样。

sentences.en: This can affect the eyes and optic nerves, sometimes causing permanent vision problems for astronauts who stay in space for months,
sentences.zh: 这会影响眼睛和视神经，有时会导致在太空中呆了几个月的宇航员出现永久性视力问题，

sentences.en: a condition called space-flight-associated neuroocular syndrome.
sentences.zh: 这种情况称为太空飞行相关神经眼科综合症。

sentences.en: It also causes fluid to accumulate in nearby tissues, giving you a puffy face and congested sinuses.
sentences.zh: 它还会导致液体在附近的组织中积聚，使你面部浮肿，鼻窦充血。

sentences.en: As with a bad cold, the process inhibits nerve endings in the nasal passages, meaning you can't smell or taste very well.
sentences.zh: 就像重感冒一样，这个过程会抑制鼻腔中的神经末梢，意味着你无法很好地闻到或尝到味道。

sentences.en: The nose plays an important role in taste.
sentences.zh: 鼻子在味觉中起着重要作用。

sentences.en: The ISS galley is often stocked with wasabi and hot sauce.
sentences.zh: 国际空间站的厨房里经常备有芥末和辣酱。

sentences.en: These sensory deficits can be helpful in some respects, though, because the ISS tends to smell like body odor or farts.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些感觉缺陷在某些方面可能很有用，因为国际空间站往往闻起来像体味或屁味。

sentences.en: You can't shower, and microgravity prevents digestive gases from rising out of the stew of other juices in your stomach and intestines, making it hard to belch without barfing.
sentences.zh: 你不能洗澡，微重力阻止了消化气体从胃和肠道中其他液体的混合物中上升，这使得打嗝而不呕吐变得很困难。

sentences.en: Because the gas must exit somehow, the frequency and volume, metric and decibel, of flatulence increases.
sentences.zh: 因为气体必须以某种方式排出，所以肠胃气胀的频率和体积、度量和分贝都有所增加。

sentences.en: Other metabolic processes are similarly disturbed.
sentences.zh: 其他代谢过程也会受到类似的干扰。

sentences.en: Urine adheres to the bladder wall rather than collecting at the base, where the growing pressure of liquid above the urethra usually alerts us when the organ is two-thirds full.
sentences.zh: 尿液附着在膀胱壁上，而不是聚集在底部，通常情况下，尿道上方不断增加的液体压力会提醒我们器官已经有三分之二满了。

sentences.en: Thus, the bladder may reach maximum capacity before an urge is felt, at which point urination may happen suddenly and spontaneously,
sentences.zh: 因此，膀胱可能会在感觉到尿意之前达到最大容量，在这一点上，排尿可能会突然且自发地发生，

sentences.en: according to A Review of Challenges and Opportunities, Variable and Partial Gravity for Human Habitats in L.E.O., or Low Earth Orbit.
sentences.zh: 根据近地轨道人类栖息地的可变和部分重力：挑战与机遇回顾。

sentences.en: This is a report that came out last year from the authors Ronke Olabasi, an associate professor of biomedical engineering at the University of California, Irvine,
sentences.zh: 这是一份去年发布的报告，作者是加州大学尔湾分校生物医学工程副教授龙克·奥拉巴西，

sentences.en: and Mae Jemison, a retired NASA astronaut.
sentences.zh: 以及退役的美国宇航局宇航员梅·杰米森。

sentences.en: Sometimes the bladder fills but doesn't empty, and astronauts need to catheterize themselves.
sentences.zh: 有时膀胱满了但排不空，宇航员需要自己导尿。

sentences.en: The longer astronauts stay in microgravity, the more they change.
sentences.zh: 宇航员在微重力下呆的时间越长，他们改变得就越多。

sentences.en: Because they don't need to support any weight, bones and muscles begin to atrophy, much faster than they do in advanced age on Earth.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不需要支撑任何体重，骨骼和肌肉开始萎缩，比他们在地球上年老时萎缩的速度快得多。

sentences.en: Bone density in the hips and spine can decrease by 1-2% per month in space, compared with 0.5-1% per year in elderly Earthlings.
sentences.zh: 在太空中，臀部和脊椎的骨密度每月可下降 1-2%，而老年地球人每年下降 0.5-1%。

sentences.en: The calcium that leaches from the bones is expelled in urine, increasing the risk of kidney stones.
sentences.zh: 从骨骼中浸出的钙会随尿液排出，从而增加患肾结石的风险。

sentences.en: Muscle mass ebbs too.
sentences.zh: 肌肉质量也会随之减少。

sentences.en: Astronauts must exercise vigorously for more than two hours a day to keep in decent shape.
sentences.zh: 宇航员必须每天进行两个多小时的高强度锻炼，才能保持良好的体型。

sentences.en: They also must constantly dab their skin with a towel while doing so, to prevent their sweat from beating and floating into colleagues or equipment.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他们还必须不断用毛巾擦拭皮肤，以防止汗水聚集成滴并漂浮到同事或设备上。

sentences.en: The discs between their spinal vertebrae spread farther apart.
sentences.zh: 脊椎骨之间的椎间盘会进一步拉开。

sentences.en: Astronauts grow taller, but their lower backs hurt.
sentences.zh: 宇航员的身高会变高，但他们的下背部会疼痛。

sentences.en: The body's sensors that on Earth raise our blood pressure when we stand up from lying down so that we don't faint grow lazy with disuse.
sentences.zh: 身体中那些在地球上当我们从躺姿站起时会提高血压以防我们晕厥的感受器，会因为废用而变得懒惰。

sentences.en: This degeneration, along with reduced muscle mass, is why astronauts must be carried from their capsules when they return to terra firma after a long mission.
sentences.zh: 这种退化加上肌肉质量的减少，就是为什么宇航员在执行长期任务返回地球表面时，必须被从返回舱中抬出来的原因。

sentences.en: The body recalibrates to normal.
sentences.zh: 身体会重新校准恢复正常。

sentences.en: But protracted stays in microgravity, the current record, 437 days, was set by the Russian astronaut Valery Polykov in 1995, make for painful recoveries.
sentences.zh: 但在失重状态下的长期停留（目前的记录是1995年由俄罗斯宇航员瓦列里·波利亚科夫创下的437天）会带来痛苦的恢复过程。

sentences.en: After 340 days in space,
sentences.zh: 在太空待了340天之后，

sentences.en: Scott Kelly, a NASA veteran of three previous shorter missions, described the period immediately following his return as much, much worse than those of earlier trips.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·凯利作为曾执行过三次较短任务的NASA老兵，将他返回后不久的那段时期描述为比以往的太空之旅糟糕得多、得多。

sentences.en: All of my joints and all of my muscles are protesting the crushing pressure of gravity, he wrote in his 2017 memoir, Endurance.
sentences.zh: 我在2017年的回忆录《坚韧》中写道：我所有的关节和肌肉都在抗议重力那沉重的压迫感。

sentences.en: Legend has it that Polykov, for his part, strolled out of his capsule, unfazed, bummed a cigarette from a friend, and started smoking.
sentences.zh: 传说波利亚科夫面不改色地走出了返回舱，向朋友借了支烟，然后开始抽了起来。

sentences.en: Of course, recovery, in this case, in every case so far, means re-acclimating to Earth's pull.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这种情况下、在迄今为止的所有情况下，恢复都意味着重新适应地球的引力。

sentences.en: But what if you never come back, and instead, stay in orbit, or on the moon, or Mars, for the rest of your life?
sentences.zh: 但如果你永远不回来，而是余生都留在轨道上、月球上或火星上呢？

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中度过的七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 Super Sundays.
sentences.zh: 60个超级星期日。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是每年联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天使用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe, because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢用一个平底锅就能做好的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world, and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您理解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer, at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅享受特惠，网址为 nytimes.com 里的 subscribe。

sentences.en: If you spin a bucket of water around your head fast enough, the water doesn't spill out.
sentences.zh: 如果你绕着头快速转动一桶水，水是不会洒出来的。

sentences.en: The same physics underpin most plans for creating what is colloquially referred to as artificial gravity.
sentences.zh: 同样的物理原理支撑着大多数旨在创造通常所说的人工重力的计划。

sentences.en: In those scenarios, the space travelers are the water.
sentences.zh: 在这些设想中，太空旅行者就是水。

sentences.en: The tricky part is that the speed at which you spin them must be faster the closer they get to the axis.
sentences.zh: 棘手的部分在于，他们离轴心越近，你旋转他们的速度就必须越快。

sentences.en: In other words, you can have either a gigantic spacecraft that rotates slowly, or a small one that rotates rapidly.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你可以拥有一个旋转缓慢的巨大航天器，或者一个旋转迅速的小型航天器。

sentences.en: Engineering and transporting such an apparatus into low-Earth orbit has so far not been a major priority for government agencies.
sentences.zh: 将这样一套装置设计并运送到近地轨道，迄今为止并不是政府机构的首要任务。

sentences.en: It's much easier and cheaper to give astronauts tools to manage their weightlessness.
sentences.zh: 给宇航员提供应对失重状态的工具要容易得多，也便宜得多。

sentences.en: But just because NASA hasn't used spinning vessels to simulate gravity doesn't mean it's not possible, says Rhonda Stevenson, the chief executive of Above Space.
sentences.zh: 但 Above Space 的首席执行官朗达·史蒂文森表示，这并不意味着 NASA 没有使用旋转容器来模拟重力就是不可能的。

sentences.en: Once it raises the necessary funding, her company plans to put a small luxury hotel into orbit within five years, and have a larger facility operational within another ten years.
sentences.zh: 一旦筹集到必要的资金，她的公司计划在五年内将一座小型豪华酒店送入轨道，并在另一个十年内让一个更大的设施投入运营。

sentences.en: In renderings, these establishments look like giant gears with rooms in their cogs.
sentences.zh: 在效果图中，这些建筑看起来像巨大的齿轮，房间就在齿轮的轮齿里。

sentences.en: Folks don't realize where we are right now and how technologically advanced we are today, she told me.
sentences.zh: 她对我说，人们没有意识到我们现在身处何地，以及我们今天的技术有多么先进。

sentences.en: Stevenson's priorities, like those of other space tourism operators, are oriented toward fun and comfort, not forbearance and science.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森的优先事项与其他太空旅游运营商一样，侧重于乐趣和舒适，而不是克制和科学。

sentences.en: Astronauts never complain, but paying guests love an excuse to leave a one-star review, especially when they'll be shelling out millions for a weekend stay.
sentences.zh: 宇航员从不抱怨，但付费的客人很喜欢找借口给出一星差评，尤其是当他们要为周末住宿花费数百万美元时。

sentences.en: In other words, there must be amenities and flush toilets, a contraption whose evolution was also guided by gravity.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，必须有配套设施和抽水马桶，这种装置的演变同样受到了重力的引导。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to go up there and be lonely and eat algae paste and crickets,
sentences.zh: 没有人想去那里感到孤独并吃藻类糊糊和蟋蟀，

sentences.en: Stevenson says.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森说。

sentences.en: That just doesn't sound like a good time.
sentences.zh: 那听起来可真不怎么好玩。

sentences.en: Eventually, such wealthy vacationers will want somewhere to go, a space mall, a mini golf course, and they'll want cosmopolitan cuisine.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些富有的度假者会想要去某个地方，比如太空商场、迷你高尔夫球场，而且他们还会想要世界各地的美食。

sentences.en: Stevenson and others predict that commercial parks, factories, and farms will all be built in space to meet their demands.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文森和其他人预测，为了满足他们的需求，商业公园、工厂和农场都将在太空中建造。

sentences.en: The hospitality industry is not the only one with space aspirations.
sentences.zh: 酒店业并不是唯一一个有太空抱负的行业。

sentences.en: Chemistry and drug discovery might thrive there.
sentences.zh: 化学和药物发现在那里可能会蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: Crystals, like those used in pharmaceuticals, grow bigger and more symmetrically in microgravity.
sentences.zh: 晶体（如药物中使用的晶体）在微重力环境下会长得更大、更对称。

sentences.en: There are ambitions to mine the moon for rare metals.
sentences.zh: 人们还有在月球上开采稀有金属的雄心。

sentences.en: Solar energy production could flourish in the absence of weather.
sentences.zh: 在没有天气干扰的情况下，太阳能发电可能会蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: And astrobotany, which will be needed to supply space settlements with fresh food, could eventually grow crops and send them back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 太空植物学将为太空定居点提供新鲜食物，它最终可以种植农作物并将其送回地球。

sentences.en: In one experiment, wheat plants grew 10% taller in microgravity.
sentences.zh: 在一项实验中，小麦植株在微重力下长高了10%。

sentences.en: When that day comes, whether you're in space working or vacationing, tuning your gravity could become part of your 9 to 5, like adjusting your thermostat.
sentences.zh: 当那一天到来时，无论你是在太空中工作还是度假，调节重力都可能成为你朝九晚五生活的一部分，就像调节恒温器一样。

sentences.en: You might spend your workday in microgravity.
sentences.zh: 你的工作时间可能是在微重力下度过的。

sentences.en: Then you might go for a jog, or just rest in 1G.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以去慢跑，或者只是在1G（一个地球重力）下休息。

sentences.en: Maybe as you age and your joints start aching, you move to rooms in 0.75G, where gravity is tempered just enough to put the spring back in your step.
sentences.zh: 也许随着你年龄的增长和关节开始酸痛，你搬到了0.75G的房间里，那里的重力得到了适度的调节，足以让你的步伐恢复活力。

sentences.en: Senior living in space.
sentences.zh: 太空高级生活。

sentences.en: Even if gravity doesn't prove quite so easy to supply as envisioned, weightlessness would mostly be just an inconvenience for the few hours it takes to get into low Earth orbit
sentences.zh: 即使重力不像想象的那样容易提供，对于进入近地轨道所需的区区几小时

sentences.en: or the few days' flight to the moon.
sentences.zh: 或是飞往月球的几天飞行来说，失重大多也只是一种不便。

sentences.en: But getting to Mars or back again will, at least at first, most likely require living in microgravity for more than a year.
sentences.zh: 但要去火星或返回地球，至少在最初，很可能需要在微重力环境中生活一年以上。

sentences.en: This raises physical concerns.
sentences.zh: 这引发了身体上的担忧。

sentences.en: Will those astronauts be able to stand up when they arrive?
sentences.zh: 这些宇航员到达时能站立吗？

sentences.en: If they can stand, will they pass out?
sentences.zh: 如果他们能站立，会晕倒吗？

sentences.en: If they pass out, will they break a bone?
sentences.zh: 如果他们晕倒了，会骨折吗？

sentences.en: And if they break a bone, will it heal as it would on Earth?
sentences.zh: 如果他们骨折了，能像在地球上一样愈合吗？

sentences.en: Researchers understand even less about astronauts' neurological states and whether cognition is affected by the pressure that fluids shifting headward put on the brain.
sentences.zh: 研究人员对宇航员的神经状态以及液体向头部转移所产生的压力是否会影响认知，了解得甚至更少。

sentences.en: Few of the NASA astronauts want to volunteer to stick a needle in their brain or eye to measure pressure while in space, Donneville says.
sentences.zh: 唐内维尔说，很少有 NASA 的宇航员愿意主动要求在太空中把针扎进他们的大脑或眼睛来测量压力。

sentences.en: It's a risk, and they are afraid we might find something that might prevent them, for medical reasons, from being able to fly.
sentences.zh: 这是一种风险，他们担心我们可能会发现某种原因，从医学角度阻止他们飞行。

sentences.en: We've had this experiment on the books for years.
sentences.zh: 我们这个实验在案子上已经放了好多年了。

sentences.en: Researchers are hoping that commercial spaceflight passengers will be more amenable to volunteering for experiments, like having a new kind of pressure transducer
sentences.zh: 研究人员希望商业航天乘客会更愿意自愿参加实验，比如在起飞前的几个月里

sentences.en: surgically implanted inside their skull in the months before takeoff.
sentences.zh: 在头骨内通过手术植入一种新型压力传感器。

sentences.en: If the device works as expected, it will answer long-standing questions about the impacts of microgravity inside the cranium.
sentences.zh: 如果该设备按预期工作，它将解答关于颅内微重力影响的长期疑问。

sentences.en: And it might also lead to insights that could help parents and doctors treat babies with hydrocephalus, a neurological disorder caused by a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid
sentences.zh: 它还可能带来一些见解，帮助父母和医生治疗脑积水婴儿，这是一种由脑深部脑室中

sentences.en: in ventricles deep within the brain.
sentences.zh: 脑脊液积聚引起的神经系统疾病。

sentences.en: Scott Kelly's mission on the ISS, nearly a year long, was designed to learn what might happen to astronauts during a flight to Mars.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·凯利在国际空间站上长达近一年的任务，旨在了解宇航员在飞往火星期间可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: It took advantage of a unique scientific opportunity.
sentences.zh: 它利用了一个独特的科学机遇。

sentences.en: Kelly has an identical twin brother,
sentences.zh: 凯利有一个同卵双胞胎兄弟，

sentences.en: Mark Kelly, a retired astronaut and now a senator from Arizona.
sentences.zh: 马克·凯利，他是一名退休宇航员，现在是亚利桑那州的参议员。

sentences.en: While Scott Kelly went to space, a genetic replica of him, or close to it, stayed behind.
sentences.zh: 当斯科特·凯利飞向太空时，他的基因复制品（或与之非常接近的人）留在了地面上。

sentences.en: When he returned, researchers compared the two men at a molecular level to see what had changed in Scott, but not in Mark.
sentences.zh: 他返回后，研究人员在分子水平上对两人进行了比较，看看斯科特身上发生了什么变化而马克身上没有。

sentences.en: Soon, we might be able to do this kind of experiment by using stem cells from an astronaut's blood to grow mini-organs that can be exposed to high levels of radiation
sentences.zh: 不久之后，我们或许就能利用宇航员血液中的干细胞来培育微型器官，从而进行这种实验，这些微型器官可以暴露在太空中的高水平辐射

sentences.en: or microgravity in space, which should show how the astronauts' actual organs would react to off-world living.
sentences.zh: 或微重力环境中，这应该能显示出宇航员真正的器官会对域外生活做出怎样的反应。

sentences.en: Our thinking was, in the future, each astronaut could give us a few milliliters of blood and we could make a platform for each individual,
sentences.zh: 我们的想法是，在未来，每个宇航员都可以给我们提供几毫升血液，我们可以为每个人定制一个平台，

sentences.en: Gordana Vyunjak-Novakovich, a professor of biomedical engineering and medical sciences at Columbia University, told me.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学生物医学工程和医学科学教授戈尔达娜·维云亚克-诺瓦科维奇对我说。

sentences.en: Space appeared to remodel Scott Kelly in subtle but perhaps significant ways.
sentences.zh: 太空似乎以微妙但或许意义重大的方式重塑了斯科特·凯利。

sentences.en: He incurred a small amount of DNA damage, believed to be caused by radiation exposure.
sentences.zh: 他的DNA受到了一定程度的损伤，据信这是由辐射暴露引起的。

sentences.en: Astronauts' radiation doses are tracked over their lifetime.
sentences.zh: 宇航员一生中的辐射剂量都会被追踪。

sentences.en: If these become too high, they can no longer go to space.
sentences.zh: 如果这些剂量变得过高，他们就不能再进入太空了。

sentences.en: He also experienced epigenetic changes, modifications in how genes are expressed that can be heritable, a feature that helps humans and other creatures preserve useful adaptations
sentences.zh: 他还经历了表观遗传学的变化，即基因表达方式的修饰，这些修饰是可以遗传的，这一特征有助于人类和其他生物保留有用的适应性，

sentences.en: without waiting for evolution to do its brutal work.
sentences.zh: 而无需等待进化去完成它残酷的工作。

sentences.en: Those alterations, which reverted nearly to their baseline state after Kelly's return, gave scientists a sense of what genes might be most impacted by lengthier stays in space.
sentences.zh: 这些改变在凯利返回后几乎恢复到了基线状态，它们让科学家们了解到哪些基因可能受太空长期停留的影响最大。

sentences.en: One of the most puzzling changes researchers observed was in his gut microbiome, as the community of bacteria, fungi, and viruses that live in the digestive tract is known.
sentences.zh: 研究人员观察到的最令人费解的变化之一是他的肠道微生物组，也就是生活在消化道中的细菌、真菌和病毒群落。

sentences.en: The species of bacteria were the same, but their proportions in relation to one another had shifted considerably, probably in part because the food Kelly ate was quite different.
sentences.zh: 细菌的种类是一样的，但它们彼此之间的比例发生了相当大的变化，这可能部分是因为凯利吃的食物有很大不同。

sentences.en: Such rearrangements among the microorganisms could be a cause for concern, because they are involved in digestion, metabolism, and immunity, and changes to their composition
sentences.zh: 微生物之间的这种重新排列可能会引起人们的担忧，因为它们参与了消化、新陈代谢和免疫，其组成的改变

sentences.en: have been associated with neurological and physiological conditions.
sentences.zh: 已经与神经和生理状况联系在一起。

sentences.en: Reduced immunity could be especially dangerous in space, where microgravity also appears to cause bacterial cell membranes to thicken and make bacteria
sentences.zh: 免疫力下降在太空中可能尤其危险，因为微重力似乎也会导致细菌细胞膜变厚，使细菌

sentences.en: more resistant to antibiotics and more likely to cause severe disease.
sentences.zh: 对抗生素更有抵抗力，并且更有可能引发严重疾病。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies, I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个字谜，我喜欢恐怖电影，喜欢我的狗，还喜欢捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis, and I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马苏斯基，我每天都创作“拼写蜜蜂”和“信箱”游戏，我有一种叫做联觉的奇特现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com 里的 games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: There will, of course, be surprises out there, some of them sure to be quite unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 当然，太空中会有惊喜，其中一些肯定会非常令人不快。

sentences.en: Jan Stepanek at the Mayo Clinic points out that scientists once thought blood clots were very unlikely to occur in the absence of Earth's gravity.
sentences.zh: 梅奥诊所的扬·斯捷潘内克指出，科学家们曾认为在没有地球重力的情况下极不可能发生血栓。

sentences.en: But then, one appeared.
sentences.zh: 但后来，血栓真的出现了。

sentences.en: In fact, in a 2019 study, an international group of researchers reported that the blood flow in the jugular veins of six of 11 ISS crew members they monitored
sentences.zh: 事实上，在2019年的一项研究中，一组国际研究人员报告称，他们监测的11名国际空间站机组人员中，有6人的颈静脉血流

sentences.en: had, by around day 50 in space, either stagnated or reverse direction.
sentences.zh: 在太空大约第50天时，已经停滞或逆转了方向。

sentences.en: And one of the six had a potentially fatal thrombosis with no symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 这六人中有一人患上了可能致命的血栓且没有症状。

sentences.en: Luckily, physicians had already stocked the ISS with a 40-day emergency supply of anticoagulants, among other medications, just in case.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，以防万一，内科医生已经在国际空间站备好了40天的抗凝剂等应急药物。

sentences.en: Space medicine experts are adept at imagining dire scenarios.
sentences.zh: 太空医学专家擅长想象可怕的场景。

sentences.en: What if somebody develops appendicitis, says Natasha Cho, an emergency medical physician and professor of aerospace medicine at the University of Texas medical branch.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯大学医学分部急诊医学医生兼航天医学教授娜塔莎·赵说，如果有人得了阑尾炎怎么办？

sentences.en: If we go to Mars, you can't pull a U-turn.
sentences.zh: 如果我们去火星，你是无法掉头的。

sentences.en: Do you send a surgeon?
sentences.zh: 你要派一名外科医生去吗？

sentences.en: What if they are the one who gets appendicitis?
sentences.zh: 如果得阑尾炎的恰好就是那个外科医生呢？

sentences.en: She and other flight surgeons are mindful of the case of a 27-year-old Soviet doctor,
sentences.zh: 她和其他航空航天外科医生都记得27岁苏联医生列昂尼德·罗戈佐夫的案例，

sentences.en: Leonid Rogozev, who in 1961 had to give himself an appendectomy at a base that he and a team of 11 others built in Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 他在1961年不得不给自己做阑尾切除手术，地点是他和另外11人团队在南极洲建立的一个基地里。

sentences.en: He did it by feel, after finding the inverted images in a mirror disorienting.
sentences.zh: 在发现镜子里的倒影让人方向感错乱后，他是凭手感完成手术的。

sentences.en: Within two hours, he had removed the infected organ and sutured himself up.
sentences.zh: 在两个小时内，他切除了感染的器官并给自己缝合了伤口。

sentences.en: A helpful colleague snapped photographs for posterity.
sentences.zh: 一位乐于助人的同事为后人拍下了照片。

sentences.en: UTMB often sends trainees in aerospace medicine to practice at a research station in Antarctica, an environment in which doctors may be called upon to perform medical procedures
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯大学医学分部经常派航天医学培训生去南极洲的一个研究站实习，在那样的环境中，医生可能需要执行

sentences.en: they haven't performed in many years with limited supplies.
sentences.zh: 他们多年未曾做过且物资有限的医疗程序。

sentences.en: Ronak Shaw, director of aerospace medicine at UTMB, puts the quandary this way.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯大学医学分部航天医学主任罗纳克·肖这样阐述这个困境。

sentences.en: Do you have the tools and support staff to complete those procedures?
sentences.zh: 你有完成这些程序所需的工具和支持人员吗？

sentences.en: Then, referring to the doctor on the original Star Trek, he adds, people often envision that surgical suite that Dr. McCoy had.
sentences.zh: 接着，他提到原版《星际迷航》中的医生，并补充说，人们常常想象麦考伊医生拥有的那个手术室。

sentences.en: In reality, it could cost $10,000 or more per pound to put a payload into orbit, and anything that goes on the spacecraft must earn its place at the expense of something else.
sentences.zh: 现实中，将有效载荷送入轨道每磅可能需要10,000美元甚至更多，进入航天器的任何东西都必须以牺牲其他东西为代价来赢得它的位置。

sentences.en: There's a defibrillator and a portable ultrasound on the ISS, but no CT scanner or MRI machine.
sentences.zh: 国际空间站上有除颤器和便携式超声仪，但没有CT扫描仪或核磁共振机。

sentences.en: Major surgery could result in the patient's insides floating out.
sentences.zh: 大手术可能会导致病人的内脏漂浮出来。

sentences.en: Even giving injections in space requires comprehensive planning.
sentences.zh: 甚至在太空中注射也需要全面的规划。

sentences.en: Rogozev could at least give himself Novocaine.
sentences.zh: 罗戈佐夫至少还能给自己打诺卡因麻醉药。

sentences.en: Cho was the flight surgeon for NASA astronauts on the ISS when the coronavirus vaccine became available, and she had to decide whether to send it up on a routine resupply flight.
sentences.zh: 当新冠疫苗面市时，赵曾担任国际空间站 NASA 宇航员的航空航天外科医生，她必须决定是否通过例行补给航班将其发送上去。

sentences.en: The decision involved weighing the protection of the astronauts when they landed on Earth, conceivably with compromised immunity, versus considerations about how to get liquid
sentences.zh: 这个决定涉及权衡宇航员在地球着陆时的保护（他们的免疫力可能已经受损），以及如何将液体吸入

sentences.en: into a syringe, how any side effects could make astronauts incapable of performing their duties, how to keep the vaccine cold enough, and how to dose it without wasting any.
sentences.zh: 注射器的考量、任何副作用如何可能使宇航员无法履行职责、如何保持疫苗足够的低温，以及如何在不浪费的情况下进行剂量的分配。

sentences.en: An ethical conundrum in the days when there was not enough to go around on Earth.
sentences.zh: 在地球上物资供不应求的日子里，这是一个道德难题。

sentences.en: Ultimately,
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: Cho decided they would have to wait until their return.
sentences.zh: 赵决定他们必须等到返回地球后再说。

sentences.en: It's a truism of our species that the moment we encounter a new and challenging environment, a mountaintop, say, or an airplane bathroom, we feel compelled to find out
sentences.zh: 我们这个物种有一个真理：每当我们遇到一个新的具有挑战性的环境（比如说山顶或是飞机的洗手间），我们就会情不自禁地想要找出

sentences.en: what will happen if we engage in coitus there.
sentences.zh: 如果在那里发生性行为会发生什么。

sentences.en: Naturally, then, as soon as the first billionaires check into the first space hotels, they will be thinking about becoming the inaugural members of the 250-mile-high club.
sentences.zh: 那么自然而然地，一旦第一批亿万富翁入住第一家太空酒店，他们就会考虑成为“250英里高空俱乐部”的首批成员。

sentences.en: This raises the issue.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一个问题。

sentences.en: There really aren't rules for medical experimentation in space that cover tourists' behavior.
sentences.zh: 太空中确实没有针对游客行为的医学实验规则。

sentences.en: If someone wants to have sex in space or have a baby in space, there's no framework to provide guidelines,
sentences.zh: 多里特·唐内维尔说，如果有人想在太空中发生性行为或在太空中生孩子，目前没有任何框架来提供指导方针。

sentences.en: Dorit Donneville says.
sentences.zh: 我们必须确保商业航天为优秀的科学研究提供机会。

sentences.en: We need to make sure commercial spaceflight provides opportunity for good science.
sentences.zh: 我们最不愿意看到的是它变成蛮荒西部，做出一些可能导致人员受伤或引发负面新闻并使人们反对太空旅行的愚蠢事情。

sentences.en: The last thing we want to do is have it turn into the Wild West and do stupid things that could get people hurt or create bad press and turn people against space travel.
sentences.zh: 那会损害整个行业。

sentences.en: That damages the whole industry.
sentences.zh: 这会损害整个行业。

sentences.en: So, should space travelers choose abstinence until a formal entity declares space-sex safe?
sentences.zh: 那么，在正式机构宣布太空性行为安全之前，太空旅行者是否应该选择禁欲？

sentences.en: Is it possible that this threshold has already been breached?
sentences.zh: 这种临界点是否已经被打破了？

sentences.en: Fewer than 700 people have flown to space so far, and it is often easy to identify who they are in research publications, which can make them reticent about details
sentences.zh: 迄今为止只有不到700人飞往过太空，而且在研究出版物中往往很容易认出他们是谁，这可能会让他们对那些

sentences.en: that might satisfy behaviorists.
sentences.zh: 可能会满足行为主义者的细节三缄其口。

sentences.en: In short, says Simone Dubé, a postdoctoral research fellow at the Kinsey Institute at Indiana University, we know very little about the intimacy and sexuality of astronauts.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，印第安纳大学金赛研究所的博士后研究员西蒙娜·迪贝说，我们对宇航员的亲密关系和性生活知之甚少。

sentences.en: But we do know some basics.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实了解一些基本情况。

sentences.en: There are good indications that erection and lubrication are not inhibited in space,
sentences.zh: 有很好的迹象表明，在太空中勃起和润滑并没有受到抑制，

sentences.en: Dubé says, and it appears that microgravity doesn't subject contraceptives to additional side effects.
sentences.zh: 迪贝说，而且微重力似乎也没有给避孕措施带来额外的副作用。

sentences.en: There are concerns about reproduction, however, that will have to be addressed if our species is ever to take up permanent residence somewhere else besides Earth.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们对生殖问题感到担忧，如果我们的物种有朝一日要在地球以外的某个地方永久居住，就必须解决这些问题。

sentences.en: For the most part, scientists have studied aspects of procreation in space only in animals, including fruit flies, frogs, newts, geckos, aquatic crustaceans, quails, rats, mice,
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，科学家们只在动物身上研究了太空中的生育问题，包括果蝇、青蛙、蝾螈、壁虎、水生甲壳类动物、鹌鹑、大鼠、小鼠，

sentences.en: and, intriguingly, raMs.
sentences.zh: 还有，有趣的是，公羊。

sentences.en: While producing and developing healthy embryos in space can be done, it clearly comes with considerable risks.
sentences.zh: 虽然在太空中产生和培育健康的胚胎是可行的，但它显然伴随着相当大的风险。

sentences.en: Radiation exposure damages DNA and can cause infertility and sterility in adults, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，辐射暴露会损害DNA，并可能导致成年人失去生育能力和不育。

sentences.en: Exposed embryos and fetuses appear more likely to have growth and cognitive delays, birth defects, and higher rates of newborn mortality.
sentences.zh: 暴露在辐射下的胚胎和胎儿似乎更有可能出现生长和认知迟缓、出生缺陷以及更高的新生儿死亡率。

sentences.en: Dubé is worried most of all about the psychological effects of intercourse or a lack thereof in space.
sentences.zh: 迪贝最担心的是太空中性行为或缺乏性行为所带来的心理影响。

sentences.en: What I want to draw people's attention to is that we are going to try to enact sexuality in all its complexity in a very small, remote, isolated, very small space
sentences.zh: 我想提请人们注意的是，我们将试图在一个非常狭小、偏远、孤立的极小空间里展现其全部复杂性的性生活，

sentences.en: with limited partners who are people you work with and depend on.
sentences.zh: 这里的伴侣有限，而且都是你共事并依赖的人。

sentences.en: Historically, in analogous situations like military basic training, this has proved disastrous, mostly for women.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，在诸如军事基础训练之类的类似情况中，这已被证明是灾难性的，对女性而言尤其如此。

sentences.en: I'm much more worried about the next morning after people have sex, how it's going to affect the crew dynamic,
sentences.zh: 我更担心的是人们发生性行为后的第二天早上，它将如何影响机组人员的动态，

sentences.en: Dubé told me, rather than are people going to be able to have sex or masturbate in the space station.
sentences.zh: 迪贝告诉我，而不是人们是否能够在空间站里发生性行为或自慰。

sentences.en: The potential adverse health effects of loneliness and isolation in space have also been understudied, but will most likely become more significant the longer a mission lasts.
sentences.zh: 太空中孤独和孤立对健康的潜在不利影响也一直研究不足，但任务持续时间越长，这些影响很可能就越显著。

sentences.en: Being in space is like the pandemic lockdowns many people experienced in 2020, except you can't open a window or take a walk outdoors.
sentences.zh: 身处太空就像许多人在2020年经历的疫情封锁一样，只是你无法打开窗户或去户外散步。

sentences.en: And the farther you get from Earth, the more lag time there is between when you send a message and when your loved one back home receives it.
sentences.zh: 而且你离地球越远，你发送消息与家乡的爱人收到消息之间的时间差就越大。

sentences.en: On Mars, the wait might be 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在火星上，等待时间可能长达20分钟。

sentences.en: NASA issued a report examining psychosocial well-being and performance in isolated, confined, and extreme environments that considered data from submarines, underground bunkers,
